minutes_text:
LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  January 24, 2023

1. A meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by Chair
  Crosby at 6:30 p.m.

  Executive Board Members present:

  Executive Board
  Rick Crosby, YFAC Chair, Mayor Pro Tem
  Wendy Lau, YFAC Vice Chair, Council Member
  Denise Fisher, Resident
  Greg Palatto, BUSD Board Member
  Don Kendrick, Resident

  Chris Dransfeldt, LVPD
  Ryan Lehotsky, LVPD
  Carlos Flores, LVPD
  Eddie Burgos, LVPD
  Hollie Savage, LVPD
  Joy Lindsay, BUSD
  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne
  Erin Beilstein, City of La Verne
  Robin Carder, Resident
  Patti Latourelle, Resident
  Isabelle Huber, WCUSD

2. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the December 6th meeting were approved.

3. Intro of New City Manager  Ken Domer, City Manager, introduced himself sharing
  that he enjoys seeing the community from different
  perspectives. He is interested in meeting with any
  group in the community who wants to talk. Don
  Kendrick shared with the group and Ken the history of
  YFAC over the past 30 years, noting that YFAC is
  adaptable and creates programs to respond to
  community needs.

4. BUSD Report  Mark Rodgers, BUSD, talked with the group about the
  return to normalcy as compared to last year given that
  January 2022 the district had over 700 cases of
  COVID-19 and this January only saw 55 cases.
  Though COVID isn’t over, the school year and whole
  world is not like it was last year. The district is bringing
  back the Spelling Bee after a 2 year hiatus which will
  be on February 6th at 5pm. New student registration is
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes January 24, 2023, page 2

  coming up including an expanded TK program at all
  elementary schools. There is an interdisciplinary team
  on crisis response this year and the district is
  addressing how to see the signs of crisis, notice risk,
  and provide care for students as soon as possible.
  Additionally, Mark shared that the educators are
  working on responding to the ChatGPT program and
  what it means to have academic honesty and how they
  can teach the students and monitor the work.

5. SRO Report  School Resource Officer, Eduardo Burgos has
  completed SRO training and is enjoying the role, while
  getting to know the staff and students. SRO Burgos
  and Tobacco Education Compliance Officer Ryan
  Lehotsky have been doing walkthroughs and vape
  education at Bonita High School and Ramona Middle
  School. They are developing relationships with
  students and working on building trust. They shared
  that vaping seems to be going down from what it used
  to be and are working on educating the students who
  are caught with vapes and their parents on safety and
  prevention.

6. Youth Internet Safety  Detective Carlos Flores of the La Verne Police
  Department shared a presentation on Youth Internet
  Safety. Detective Flores is part of the Internet Crimes
  Against Children task force and shared his expertise on
  how to keep students safe online. He stressed that it is
  important for parents and students to monitor
  connections, what they share, and the communications
  that are sent. A lot of the online internet abuse is aimed
  at getting money and blackmail the child, and the
  interactions end in money transfers via Zelle or
  CashApp to overseas accounts. It's important that the
  youth feel safe with adults and that adults focus on
  listening and not judging when situations arise.
  Detective Flores also shared that it is important to teach
  students to be assertive when something doesn’t feel
  right and that anything put on the internet can affect
  their future paths and careers. There are also signs of
  students who are being bullied and adults should
  educate themselves on what those are. Lastly,
  Detective Flores shared that he will be doing an internet
  safety presentation at Ramona Middle School as well.

7. Public Comment  Don Kendrick shared with the group about the bullying
  article that he attached to the agenda. The group

  discussed what it would look like to bring forward
  restorative solutions in our community.

8. Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting was scheduled for February
  28, 2023.

9. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 7:24 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Erin Beilstein
Management Analyst
